cec2a8e7a175ade89ce5588e47697f212d98e2a9.summary: A 2018 blog post by MlwrDssctng describes a debugger-based method for exporting the configuration of the JRAT/Adwind malware. The post says the malware creates a decoy JAR and config before running the real ones. It names x32dbg as the debugger used. No actors, CVEs or figures are named.

techniques.q: creates a fake JAR and config at the beginning to confuse analysts.

audit_history.note: summary: Says the malware 'first creates a fake JAR and config ... then starts several processes, including checks for AV products via WMI'. The text says JRAT

ceb6daf589923566e4096f2c089c89605ceaf8eb.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group tracks UNC6040, a financially motivated cluster that uses voice phishing to get employees to connect a modified Salesforce Data Loader to their Salesforce environment. After access it exfiltrates Salesforce data and moves laterally into platforms such as Okta, Workplace and Microsoft 365. Extortion can follow months later, with the actor claiming ShinyHunters affiliation. Google recommends restricting API-enabled permissions, limiting app installation authorization and blocking commercial VPNs. Salesforce says the attacks are social engineering, not a…
